title: LEBRE research record — v0.54
description:
Research record of LEBRE (Lifecycle-governed Evidence-Based Resource Evolution), an online one-step-ahead forecaster for time series with inputs, at a counted cost per step. Its structural core accepts each structural change (adding, removing, swapping or refining the response to a whole input) by an anytime-valid sequential test (e-process) of predictive improvement, within an online multiple-testing procedure. Layer M1 adds a precision expert combined with the core by AdaHedge; layer M2 starts the forecast from a declared trivial reference (zero, persistence or seasonal naive) and combines two paths by an (A,B)-Prod.

Version v0.54 extends the principle “change only with evidence, at a known cost” to cost and to the exit of structure: M1 sleeps while its weight is negligible and wakes by evidence (M5a); the report of equivalent inputs becomes cheap (M5b); a removal test with per-episode evidence and its own error budget opens when a unit's contribution drops (M4). It was promoted on 2026-10-13 by a pre-registered rule: on 93 series reserved before any v0.54 code (basins, buildings, wind and solar plants, EIA price and US Treasury rate levels), no family was harmed against v0.53 (error ratio 0.989 to 1.000) and the median per-series cost was 0.905 of v0.53's (95% CI 0.857-0.932). A post-promotion stress audit found no correctness defect nor catastrophic failure; errata 01 fixed a per-step cost peak with identical forecasts and declared a limit (relations that disappear for more than about 5,200 steps and return are removed and must be re-detected).

This archive contains the Python reference implementations, a C99 port of the core with firmware and scripts for a simulated Cortex-M4F microcontroller (Renode), experiment scripts, pre-registrations, result tables, reports, frozen versions with SHA-256 manifests (v0.1, v0.51, v0.52, v0.53, v0.54), the self-contained v0.54 specification (English and Portuguese) and scripts to verify integrity and reproduce results. Development and validations are in the public LEBRE Lab (https://github.com/Iquitim/lebre-lab). Raw third-party data, per-series prediction arrays and toolchains are not included; they are listed with SHA-256 in docs/research/ARTIFACTS_MANIFEST.tsv.

Scope and limits. One-step forecasting; the cost cut of v0.54 is about 10% at the median (none where M1 helps); spurious inputs in level series are still accepted and the cycle must still be declared; no formal error guarantee in the original scale for M1 and M2; microcontroller costs only for the core and from a simulator; the core's testing mechanism did not improve accuracy over an all-inputs-on ablation; no component is original. See the specification, section 22.
